summary: The current low-body Stegosaurus primary already has the most natural tail-tip read among this loop. A local four-spike guide aligned correctly with the tail, but the added rear spikes stayed faint and translucent. Low-denoise refine preserved the image but did not make the fourth spike more countable. Strict inpaint over the original low-body candidate also changed too little to justify replacing the current primary.
primaryRejectReasons: local guide variants are useful for review but read as subtle translucent overlays at crop scale
low-denoise refine outputs preserve the body but do not materially improve the tail-spike count
strict inpaint outputs stay too close to the source and do not add a clearer fourth spike
none of the outputs improve the current primary enough to offset new tail-tip uncertainty
usefulFindings: The low-body candidate should remain first for now because its body proportion is better than the round-body large-thagomizer candidate.
Tail-tip-only inpaint is too conservative at denoise 0.16 to 0.42 on this source and mask.
The next useful Stegosaurus route should use a stronger reference-conditioned tail target or a focused LoRA/synthetic expansion rather than another narrow tail-tip inpaint with the same mask.
nextRoute: Keep the low-body app primary unchanged. If continuing Stegosaurus, test a stronger tail-specific control reference or train/review synthetic Stegosaurus tail-spike seeds; do not promote the v1 guide/refine/strict outputs.
